description: “If you don't tie the knot with the person of your dreams within the next year, you'll be in big trouble.” So forewarns Urara, the self-proclaimed Goddess of Matchmaking, when she appears before our hero Hajime Kanbayashi. Just as Hajime begins to despair, Urara teaches him about three candidates potentially written into his destiny along with their respective “destiny counts,” which represent the distance he'll have to overcome to win their hearts and the goal is to reduce the number to zero.

title: ドットカレシ-We're 8bit Lovers-
difficultyExplanation: Mostly slice-of-life with JRPG words and characters. Everything is voiced, and the protagonist only talks through emoticons and the choices you make. Pretty short, so can be a first visual novel.
description: Series of three visual novels in which the protagonist gets transported in a JRPG game where she can romance different JRPG characters.

title: レムレスブルーの午前２時
difficultyExplanation: The story can be confusing, but the vocabulary is mostly slice of life. Not voiced.
description: Aoi appears to have the key to a rose that is said to bring eternal youth to the living and give life back to those who have died. What could be the secret behind this phantom flower, the "Lemures Blue", and the lost prodigy, Akane, and why does everybody want to win Aoi's heart?

title: ヨスガノソラ
difficultyExplanation: Pretty standard vocabulary, nothing too difficult jumps out. Some of the action occurs in a shrine but other than this, decently easy. Could be used as a first visual novel.
description: Two twins - Haruka and Sora, are going back to their grandfather's house. Nothing has changed. Good memories and a silent atmosphere heal the sadness.... However, the peaceful life gradually changes.... A secret promise made a long time ago. A lost treasure. The real reason for moving to the town. Feelings long kept a secret. The story now starts under the summer sun...

title: Flyable Heart
difficultyExplanation: Mostly slice of life romcom dating sim, but the story has fantasy elements which make it a tad bit harder than the average slice of life.
description: One day, an admission pamphlet to a famous academy arrived, containing an “all-you-can-eat” cafeteria pass. That alone was enough to lure our hero into visiting the super-prestigious Otori Ryouran College Community, home to students who excel in a variety of fields. Offbeat and unique students like a robot seem natural at Otori Ryouran. Organizing this odd student body is the responsibility of two groups ―― the Student Council and the Ryouran Society.

title: ATRI -My Dear Moments-
difficultyExplanation: Easy to follow story, mostly basic grammar without long sentences. All characters except for the protagonist are voiced. Most chapters are pure slice of life while the rest of them contains light to moderate amount of seafaring, science and technology (energetics, robotics) related vocabulary.
description: In the near future, a sudden and unexplained sea rise has left much of human civilization underwater. Ikaruga Natsuki, a boy who lost his mother and his leg in an accident some years earlier, returns disillusioned from a harsh life in the big city to find his old countryside home half-swallowed by the sea. Left without a family, all he has to his name is the ship and submarine left to him by his oceanologist grandmother, and her debts.

title: fault - milestone one
difficultyExplanation: Some sci-fi and fantasy stuff going on and that sweet, sweet katakana for a lot of in-universe words and names. Plot isn't terribly complex but easy to lose track of if you're not fully grasping what the characters are saying because of the sci-fi stuff. No voice acting, which might turn some people off. Part of an ongoing series, but I only read the first one, so can't give more info.
description: Selphine is princess of the kingdom of Roughzenhaide, which she has to flee with her Royal Guard Ritona after a brutal assault on the kingdom by unknown attackers. Using magic, the two of them get teleported to a place far far away, where magic has become a rarity as technology has become more advanced. They meet Rune, a mysterious woman, and become entangled in a dark family history.

title: 9RIP
difficultyExplanation: Otome game where you date ghosts. Dialogue uses easy grammar, there's an in-game dictionary for game-specific terminology that's easily accessible, and it's hookable with agent. Some words that are usually kana-only have furigana on them, and many words are repeated over and over again, so it's like natural SRS. Slice of life, with some Buddhist terminology (it's about ghosts).
description: Protagonist Misa Isshiki is a second-year high school student. It was around the beginning of fall when her best friend said this to her, which gave her a shock. “I don’t believe in being spirited away, so I’m alright.” That’s right, she doesn’t believe in it. She just… feels lost because of a major distress—her career path. She hears a creepy voice whisper in her ears. “Let us find your path. I am the one who will tempt you into the darkness.”

title: 夢見鳥
difficultyExplanation: While slice of life, the lines are long and there are difficulty spikes here and there.
description: Makoto ended up living with his brother after his parents moved abroad for work, but his life keeps going wrong... But he won't be able to figure it out until it's too late. This a BL visual novel full of yandere boys.

title: 白昼夢の青写真
difficultyExplanation: For the most part standard written VN language with some slightly more difficult SF parts at a few times. Difficulty spike at the end.
description: 3 different stories spanning through very different settings with romance as their base but each different in nature, eventually accumulating in a true route rich in plot, worldbuilding and moving at its core. The production in terms of music, art and writing is stellar. Probably the most universally liked and also captivating VN I know.

title: Steins;Gate
difficultyExplanation: Overall easy vocab and grammar besides some science terms in the beginning. There's also some otaku slang and references throughout the VN. It's quite long if you want to complete all the routes however.
description: The story follows the mad scientist, Okabe Rintarou and his rag tag band of friends who discover a means of changing the past via text messages, using a modified microwave. Their experiments into how far they can go with their discovery begin to spiral out of control as they become entangled in a conspiracy surrounding SERN, the organisation behind the Large Hadron Collider, and John Titor who claims to be from a dystopian future.

title: CHAOS;HEAD NOAH
difficultyExplanation: If you've never read any chuuni novels before, the start might feel quite slow. It contains a lot of slang and some scientific vocab. The hardest part here is to endure Takumi's behavior. He has a lot of internal dialogue (which, of course, isn't voiced), and even when someone is talking to him, he'll often go off in his head for a few lines. On the plus side, there's an inbuilt lexicon for slang and some difficult vocab, which helps a lot with cultural references.
description: "If you were God, and your delusions could become reality, what delusions would you wish for? A sensual world? A despotic society? Destructive sanctions? Or..." Nishijou Takumi, a shut-in gamer and anime otaku, spends his days locked away in a shipping container while occasionally attending classes. In his place of residence, Shibuya, a bizarre string of serial killings is set in motion as he is dragged into the ordeal.

title: イハナシの魔女
difficultyExplanation: Generally slice of life vocabulary but also tends to have lore dumps, especially 琉球 culture. One chapter in particular is harder. Requires a special texthooker to hook.
description: A boy moves to a remote island in Okinawa and is informed that his grandfather, who was supposed to take care of him, has evaporated. When he is ready to fend for himself on the remote island, he meets a girl who calls herself a witch. The girl deals with magic from another world and life on a remote island where Ryukyuan culture is deeply rooted. What fate awaits them both?

title: 忠臣蔵46+1
difficultyExplanation: Set in Edo period so you get samurai Japanese and all that. It's not actually that hard to understand the plot it's just there's mentions of a lot of places and things that you'd be unfamiliar with if you don't know Japanese history. I don't think it makes the game harder to understand.
description: Protag from current era ends up in edo period in the body of someone with the same name, he passes it off as him losing his memory, and realizes he's living through the history of the 47 rounin except all of them are women instead of men. Through his interactions with them he tries to find his place among them and also struggles with his morality and trauma when it comes to fighting and potentially killing.

title: うみねこのなく頃に
difficultyExplanation: Sentences have a normal difficulty and the vocabulary isn't anything too out of the usual, though it occasionally has some challenging topics to follow, like philosophy, politics and finance being mentioned. Considering the length of the VN, those aren't commonplace.
description: The story focuses on a group of eighteen people on a secluded island for a period of two days, and the mysterious murders that befall them. Readers are challenged to discern whether the murders were committed by a human or some other, supernatural source, as well as the method and motive behind them.

title: ランス (series)
difficultyExplanation: Average difficulty sentences with a lot of fantasy elements and occasionally also historical elements but other than being very text-heavy, fairly normal for a JRPG.
description: The Rance series follows the titular character, Rance, as he saves a number of kingdoms, defeats demon invaders, and causes mischief in the in-game world, "The Continent." He has appeared in most of the main series games as the playable character, accompanied by his loyal slave, Sill Plain.

title: ドーナドーナ いっしょにわるいことをしよう
difficultyExplanation: Overall pretty normal language and a high gameplay focus for an eroge. It has some politics talk that can be challenging at times and the H-scenes themselves have more challenging language than the rest of the game.
description: Asougi City, on the Seto Inland Sea, is dominated by the corporation whose name it now shares. The Asougi Group ordains every aspect of the citizens’ lives, but as those everyday lives are peaceful, few people object or question it at all. Only one thing disturbs the city’s harmonic order: the activities of the “Anti-Aso” hunting clans, who snatch people off the streets by force and then hustle their bodies on those same streets to customers.

title: MUSICUS!
difficultyExplanation: Grammar and vocabulary are nothing special. The most distinctive characteristic is the longer sentences which seem to be a staple of the author's style. I'd imagine it can be difficult if you're not that comfortable those kinds of sentences, but a lot of them are voiced and aren't actually too complex. There are a handful of forced auto-read sections, around 4 if I'm remembering correctly, that were just way too fast but they're not too lengthy.
description: Main protagonist Tsushima Kei is asked by Yagihara, the president of a music production, to accompany their band on their upcoming tour. A few days later after that memorable first live, Kei found out that they were disbanding. Unable to accept the sudden news, he approached Korekiyo many times to convince him to change his mind, but no argument could sway him. Instead, Korekiyo asked him: “How about you play rock in my place?”

title: 扉の伝説 ～風のつばさ～
difficultyExplanation: The text is pretty simple, the difficulty mainly comes from the absurdly long text.
description: Lucia Maverick has worked as a maid in the remote village of Kast, home to many fleeing their pasts, for the last five years after the death of her parents. But her sick little sister, Anna, grows weaker by the day, and so Lucia plans to set out on a journey to Lestaria in hopes of finding employment as a Royal Guard on her fifteenth birthday, thereby securing funds for Anna's treatment. But things do not go as planned, and the return of a past terror is just the beginning of a small yet massive adventure...

title: Black Sheep Town
difficultyExplanation: Medium to Medium Hard. Like other Setoguchi VNs (Musicus, ヒラヒラヒヒル, etc.), it contains long, but digestible, sentences. The game has a lot of words that are Chinese, but there's an in-game dictionary that you can configure that highlights these words and allows you to click on them. Unfortunately, the dictionary isn't hookable with Textractor (to my knowledge), so I would recommend having a decent vocabulary before reading this.
description: BLACK SHEEP TOWN is a digital novel set in a fictional city. It is a cosmopolitan downtown area where immigrants from all over the world live, and it is full of energy with visitors who enjoy its unique atmosphere, but the other side of the city is a dangerous area where gangs rule and the police have no power. This title features a wide variety of characters with different standpoints and perspectives.

title: バット・ノット・フォー・ユー
difficultyExplanation: NVL with more literary text, but nothing unusual vocabulary wise. Sentences are longer than your average ADV VN, the text is pretty clean and has good pacing so shouldn't be too hard in any case, similar difficulty to something like Setoguchi I'd say.
description: Doujin eroge. The story starts with a short prologue with Momo, a guy who has a crush on his literature club senpai, Shiori. Sadly she doesn’t seem too interested in guys. The very next day, a Thursday, he wakes up as a girl confused what’s going on as. Everyone now recognises her as a girl, as if the male version had never existed.

title: 夢幻廻廊 [nukige]
difficultyExplanation: Vague plot with many unanswered questions left for interpretation.
description: Not for the faint of heart. Mugen Kairou, released by Black Cyc, asks the question of how our lives would be if our entire existence is based on BDSM. Taro is placed within this situation as he lives as a cattle in a mansion full of mystique. Taro's existence would be akin to that of cattle or a pet, a being completely subservient to his masters' whims and desires. As time progresses, we see the events that occur, the mysteries that unfold, and the life that Taro has decided upon.

title: ALPHA-NIGHTHAWK
difficultyExplanation: Has sci-fi terms and slightly longer sentences than average.
description: A story of political conflict as danger looms, threatening mankind's very survival. A space opera of racial and ideological disagreements as the conflicts of everyday life continue to consume our lives. And finally, a tale of hope in a desolate world as two people strive for a better future.

title: シュヴァルツェスマーケン
difficultyExplanation: Grammar overall is relatively simple which makes the sentences easier to understand, but along with the sentences being on the longer end at times, there is a lot of military vocab and 6-8 kanji-long compounds that take some getting used to. After reading it for a short while it gets easier since the same vocab is used often. If you are coming from reading unlimited/alternative muv luv in japanese then it will probably be pretty easy.
description: Related to Muv Luv. The story follows the East German Army's 666th TSF Squadron in its battles and political conflicts during the BETA's westward push in 1983. The East German Army 666th TSF Squadron "Schwarzesmarken" (Black Marks) are a special-forces unit tasked with assaulting BETA forces through unconventional tactics; specifically, they target Lux and Magnus Lux to deny the BETA the advantage of ranged firepower.

title: グランシード
difficultyExplanation: Somewhat difficult fantasy speech, uncommon expressions, elementals that speak solely in katakana, and a great deal of metaphors. The game also has some puzzles that require text input in Japanese so note taking is necessary. Dialogue text can be parsed easily with texthooking (see Neko Project II).
description: Akira Ichijou is an ordinary Japanese high-school student. One fine Sunday, he goes out to meet his lovely girlfriend Kanami. Suddenly they see a strange glowing ball. When they touch it, they enter a portal that leads to a parallel dimension named Grounseed. It is a medieval world with spirits and magic. Naturally, it was no coincidence that Akira ended up there: the balance of both worlds is in danger, and only a person from our dimension can restore it.

title: ダンガンロンパシリーズ
difficultyExplanation: The overall level of grammar and vocabulary isn't too bad, but it's important to follow the various lines of logic of the characters accurately and come to your own conclusions to advance the story.
description: Sixteen talented students who stand out in different fields are trapped by a bear-like machine, Monokuma. Monokuma traps the cast into killing games. The cast is trapped for the rest of their lives in an establishment and the only way to return home is by killing another person and avoiding being found guilty during the class trials.

title: NORN9 ~ノルン+ノネット~
difficultyExplanation: Mostly slice-of-life with all the characters being voiced except the naration/character's thoughts, but has SF and supernatural vocab, with difficulty spike at the end.
description: The story takes place a little in the future. Guided by one particular song, young elementary kid, Suzuhara Sorata is warped through a timeskip to an unfamiliar place much like the Meiji and Taisho eras from his textbooks. In this world, he meets 3 young ladies and 9 young men, and joins them on a journey aboard the mysterious ‘Norn’ ship in the sky.

title: オメガヴァンパイア
difficultyExplanation: Overall harder than a slice of life.
description: In a world in which humans and vampires coexist, the protagonist after an accident get transformed from Beta into Omega and gets tangled into the world of vampires. This is an Omegaverse BL.

title: 神学校-Noli me tangere-
difficultyExplanation: One milion characters visual novel that is overall managable, except the theological/biblical specific vocab, and some difficult spikes here and there. Good as a starter to get into the medium level visual novels.
description: On the eve of their Christmas holidays, the twins return home eager to see their family only to find them dead and their home in flames. On the wall a bizarre mark, the mark of a secret society found in their very own theological school - a secret society which worships the devil. Having forsaken God, the protagonist starts investigating in hopes of getting revenge.

title: Fate/stay night
difficultyExplanation: There are a lot of SoL scenes that are easy to read, but explanations and fight scenes which are harder to follow are just as common. Nasu's writing style may take a while to get used to, but due to the sheer length you'll be sure to be used to it by the end. Its length, topic-matter and subsequently large vocab-size might make this less suitable for most beginners but you'll have an easier time every route that you finish.
description: Multi-route-mystery, battle-royal extraordinaire that doesn't need an introduction. One of if not the most popular VN of all time: Fate/stay night. Our protagonist Shirou unsuspectingly ends up involved in the Holy Grail War and fights to the death in order to change his Fate.

title: White Album 2
difficultyExplanation: Lots of slang and long sentences, you need to follow the plot too so can be decently hard.
description: Really tense and emotional romantic drama. You will cry.

title: 月姫 -A piece of blue glass moon-
difficultyExplanation: Has a lot of chuuni vocabulary and some difficult words now and then, but overall not too bad.
description: Tsukihime chronicles the story and life of a teenage boy named Shiki Tohno. As a young boy, Shiki suffered a life-threatening injury. As a result of this injury, Shiki became able to see "death lines" on objects and people; if Shiki traces these lines with a sharp object, the person or object that they belong to will die or be destroyed.

title: 東京NECRO
difficultyExplanation: A fair amount of sci-fi terminology, including made-up words for the setting. Grammatical structure is fairly standard.
description: The ice-cold and snow-covered wasteland Tokyo of gunpowder smoke, living dead, crime and cybernetics. But in this frozen hellscape people have survived, protected by the guns and cybernetics enhancements of the Living Dead Stalkers. Now begins the battle of the living dead stalkers and the heroine with their lives at stake.

title: きっと、澄みわたる朝色よりも、
difficultyExplanation: The writer's writing style is often not very straight forward with lots of symbolism and wordplay. Many kanji puns that are important to understand for the story.
description: Set in Autumn, the main character finally meets his old friends when he enters a prestigious art school in the mountains, isolated from the rest of society. Often called "Asairo", this VN is one of the most Japanese VNs you can find. It heavily relies on Japanese mythology and themes throughout its storytelling.

title: planetarian ～ちいさなほしのゆめ～
difficultyExplanation: A very short game with an easy to follow story, using overall simple grammar and medium length sentences at most. Difficulty is raised mostly by military vocabulary as well as some astronomy-related stuff. There is one long chapter with a moderate difficulty spike (vocabulary-wise) in the latter half of the game.
description: It is thirty years after the failure of the Space Colonization Program. Humanity is nearly extinct. A perpetual and deadly Rain falls on the Earth. Men known as "Junkers" plunder goods and artifacts from the ruins of civilization. One such Junker sneaks alone into the most dangerous of all ruins—a "Sarcophagus City." In the center of this dead city, he discovers a pre-War planetarium. And as he enters he is greeted by Hoshino Yumemi, a companion robot.

title: BALDR SKY Dive 1-2
difficultyExplanation: Has some hard sci-fi dumps but a lot of words have English katakana which makes parsing easier. There is also quite a bit of action gameplay which is difficult in and of itself.
description: While Kou is asleep in his bed, the scream of a girl wakes him up. He rises to see in front of him a battle full of gunshots and flashing bombs exploding. He realizes that he is wearing an iron armor. "What's this?" He doesn't know what's going on.

title: 沙耶の唄
difficultyExplanation: Lots of low frequency, literary words, sentences arent that short either. Pretty short length-wise at least.
description: Not for the faint of heart. The story centers around Fuminori Sakisaka, a medical school student involved in a vehicle accident that claimed the lives of both his parents and left him with critical injuries. He was rescued by experimental brain surgery that coincidentally altered his perception of the world dramatically. Everything now seems to be composed of slimy intestines and gore to him. In addition, the rest of his senses: touch, hearing, smell, and taste, are also impaired.

title: 幕末尽忠報国烈士伝 MIBURO
difficultyExplanation: Mostly easy, however there are a handful of scenes where they overload you with a bunch of domain names and minor retainers or whatever which can slow you down a lot. Overall though they do dumb it down for you, even if your knowledge of Japanese history is nonexistent you will be able to keep up since the game knows natives won't be all too familiar with the content. The only stuff you have to know is stuff like who is the emperor? What does the shogunate do? What is Sekigahara?
description: It is the Bakumatsu era. There has long existed a mysterious sort of power... The legends say that this power awakens within a chosen person when the nation is on the cusp of fate. A person with this power can read an enemy's weaknesses like an open book, and can cut them down with a single stroke.

title: マツリカの炯-kEi- 天命胤異伝
difficultyExplanation: Taking place in Ancient China means that there are a lot of made up Japanese readings for Chinese words, as well as completely made up words as well but mostly limited to food. This is mitigated by the in-game dictionary, which is pretty great. The kanji isn't too insane but it's much harder than many other otome games in the same genre, and the prologue is a literal chinese poem with a nonsensical japanese translation, but it's just for flavour and doesn't actually mean anything.
description: Taking place in a world where humans, immortals, and sacred beasts coexist, the protagonist, a connoisseur living in Matsurika Village, has to come to terms with the events following her coming of age ceremony and explore her heritage and bloodline.

title: 終のステラ
difficultyExplanation: Lots of science vocab related to AI and futuristic technology, author prefers to use Kanji for common Katakana words.
description: Post apocalyptic earth far into the feature, humanity has almost been erased by "singularity machines" and technologic progress has been set back by hundreds of years. The protagonist is a transporter that goes into deserted human cities to bring back lost technology. One day he receives a request to deliver an android girl that wishes to be human to a huge space elevator that pierces the sky. Can she become human? And what awaits them at their destination?

title: 剣が君
difficultyExplanation: It has 江戸時代 vocabulary (but the in-game dictionary can assist you), arhaic usages of kanji, references and grammar; hard prologue, but the slice-of-life parts are easy to get used to; 1milion characters long. Some extra are not voiced.
description: The protagonist under the pressure of the bakufu departs on a journey with six samurai for bodyguards on a marriage promenade. On her journey, she becomes tangled up in youkai business, as well as the ‘Sword Retrieving Imperial Match’ that concerns the legendary five great swords, which is really a cover for a sickening ritual being performed…

title: うたわれるもの 偽りの仮面
difficultyExplanation: While its predecessor used a lot of obscure kanji and weird katakana words, this one seems to have more "standard" terminology. However the language is much more descriptive and elaborate and there's a lot more narrative passages and sequences compared to the first one. I'd say the level of the language is slightly harder than the previous one and people who played the first one but aren't good with visual novel language might struggle a bit more with this one.
description: Sequel to the original utawarerumono game. See the Video Games section for a description of that one.

title: 装甲悪鬼村正
difficultyExplanation: Lots of fight scenes and a good few infodumps. Quite large vocab but the text is generally easy to follow.
description: Really fun armored suit battle game that hits super hard emotionally. An all-time great.

title: いつか、届く、あの空に。
difficultyExplanation: Combination of huge vocabulary and bizarre narrative structure in the second half. Lots of kanji puns too.
description: Cool mythology game with a fun cast and some really cool aesthetics.

title: Dies irae ~Acta est Fabula~
difficultyExplanation: Has easy SoL scenes but mainly focuses on long fight scenes. Grandiose language, lots of kanji and rare words and chants. Characters speaking in a very vague manner and it being a multi-route mystery also play a part in its difficulty.
description: Quintessential uber-chuunige by Masada from the 森座万象シリーズ (also encompassing Paradise Lost and 神咒神威神楽) - if you really like chuunige you'll probably like it, if not it may not be for you.

title: 神咒神威神楽
difficultyExplanation: Has a lot of complicated vocabulary and abstract writing/depictions that are harder to interpret. Has infodumps, chuuni chants and buddhist vocabulary. Plus it's Masada which means flowery prose.
description: In ancient Ashihara no Nakatsukuni, generals fought each other to gain the favour of the emperor. They attempted to invade the uncharted eastern lands, but suffered total defeat at the hands of demons more intelligent than humans. Three hundred years later, the land of the gods, Shinshuu, has locked itself away from all foreign countries, but an air of gloom begins to drift in from the east. They are forced to head east again to drive away the demons.

title: 鬼哭街 The Cyber Slayer
difficultyExplanation: One could argue Hard would be better since the VN is actually quite short, but it is harder than anything above. Novel-like writing, complicated 漢語 to the point of using actual Chinese words, infodumps about Kung Fu and technology, immense vocabulary... Very rough. That being said the writing is great, it's just that you won't have seen these words from reading other visual novels alone.
description: In this age where technology is changing the face of combat, heirs to the ancient martial traditions have developed anti-cyborg techniques for the sole purpose of defeating cyborgs with one's bare hands. Kong Taoluo, one such master and former asssassin in the Qingyun Society, returns to Shanghai after being betrayed by the syndicate and assumed dead. Discovering what has happened to his sister during his absence; Taoluo swears an oath of vengeance and sets out to murder those responsible.

title: Famicom Detective Club
difficultyExplanation: Easy Japanese with furigana.
description: Both games revolve around a young detective trying to solve a murder case. In one game you investigate the death of a wealthy and influential local and in the other game you investigate the murder of a school student and it's a murder mystery/ghost story kind of thing.
romajiTitle: famicom detective club the two case collection

title: 妖怪ウォッチ
difficultyExplanation: Uses both beginner RPG speak and everyday language with NPCs. Has furigana on all kanji.
description: Charming, cozy RPG series with a bunch of different spin-offs. The main series is a pokemon-like in a mid-size, modern day japanese town. All the games are dirt easy, but have some fun exploration and end-game bosses.

title: あつまれどうぶつの森
difficultyExplanation: Has a lot of everyday language and is easy overall, making it great for beginners.
description: More commonly known in the West as Animal Crossing. Extremely wholesome series where you build your house and in some case village with other animal friends.

title: Snack World: The Dungeon Crawl - Gold
difficultyExplanation: The grammar is relatively simple and it’s all with furigana so kanji shouldn’t be an issue. There are a lot of puns about food (mostly) with character and enemy names. The mechanics are very simple in general and if you like dungeon crawling light-hearted action RPGs, I think you will enjoy this.
description: Crawl through randomly-generated dungeons in this roguelike RPG, delving deeper and deeper, besting brutal bosses, and hunting down rare loot. Prepare your equipment in town for the challenges that await! Head out to explore caves, woods, and other dangerous locales. Team up to topple tenacious tyrants! - Da~rling! Lookin' go~od! You are the crawler of your own dungeon!
romajiTitle: snack world the dungeon crawl gold

title: ファーランドストーリー～遠い国の物語～
difficultyExplanation: Simple fantasy vocab and not very much of it. As an SRPG, there’s some exposition and speech at the beginning and end of each level but very easy overall. Text can be parsed easily with texthooking (see Neko Project II).
description: Farland Story is the first in the row of successful Japanese strategy RPG games. The main hero of the game is a knight named Arc, who is in love with the beautiful priestess Ferio. One day, when Arc and his best friend Randia are out of town, a hostile army under the command of a mysterious Black Knight invades the town and kidnaps Ferio. Thus begins Arc's quest to defeat the enemies and to rescue his beloved one from their clutches.

title: ドラゴンクエストXオフライン
difficultyExplanation: Overall very beginner friendly and has an option to turn on furigana. The main difficulty comes from the various puns and language quirks that some characters have. Other than that should be doable but be careful as stuff like the quest log doesn't have furigana.
description: Dragon Quest X Offline (not to be confused with the online version) is a remake of the Dragon Quest X online MMO but meant to be played offline as a single player campaign. The story and world is the same as the MMO version, however the gameplay is slightly different.

title: 逆転裁判
difficultyExplanation: Mostly everyday language with the exception of some court speak. Lines of text need to be short enough for the tiny GBA screen for the first game. Can easily find japanese scripts of this game online which helps tremendously.
description: Known in the West as Ace Attorney. The player takes the roles of various defense attorneys, including Phoenix Wright, his mentor Mia Fey, and his understudies Apollo Justice and Athena Cykes, who investigate cases and defend their clients in court; they find the truth by cross-examining witnesses and finding inconsistencies between the testimonies and the evidence they have collected.

title: 遊☆戯☆王デュエルモンスターズGX タッグフォース
difficultyExplanation: Furigana on every kanji, sentences limited to two lines at most (except on the cards). The cards aren't too difficult either since they're written for kids.
description: The player enrolls at Duel Academy as a transfer student. The main focus of the game is a Tag Force tournament that will take place on the island. Players must find a partner to compete in the tournament alongside.
romajiTitle: yu gi oh gx tag force

title: スナックワールドトレジャラーズゴールド
difficultyExplanation: The grammar is relatively simple and it’s all with furigana so kanji shouldn’t be an issue. There are a lot of puns about food (mostly) with character and enemy names. The mechanics are very simple in general and if you like dungeon crawling light-hearted action RPGs, I think you will enjoy this.
description: Let the dungeon crawl...begin! After your village is invaded, become a heroic adventurer and seek revenge against the villainous Sultan Vinegar! In this RPG, crawl through randomly generated dungeons in your search for rare treasure, and team up with up to three other players in local or online multiplayer to take down tenacious tyrants!
romajiTitle: snack world the dungeon crawl gold

title: 十三機兵防衛圏
difficultyExplanation: Lots of plot devices, but the story is told from 13 perspectives often revolving around the same events, so the same events are discussed several times with similar vocabulary, which makes it easier.
description: The game tells 13 distinct stories - one for each of it's 13 characters. However the fate of the 13 characters intersects at many points making up an overarching storyline about saving the world spanning over many centuries.

title: ペーパーマリオ オリガミキング
difficultyExplanation: The game has full furigana support and is relatively easy to follow. There’s a few instances of weird speech (either archaic or some other speech quirks) but for the most part it shouldn’t be too hard. There are a few word puzzles and trivia with wordplays that might get tricky but it’s a good test of understanding.
description: The Switch entry in the Paper Mario series which blends RPG, puzzle and action-adventure elements with the traditional Mario cast.

title: ポケモン不思議のダンジョン救助隊DX
difficultyExplanation: Has a lot of standard JRPG terminology but dialogue and such is easy.
description: Pokémon Mystery Dungeon games are based in dungeons (“mystery dungeons”) where a floor map is randomly generated. In the dungeons, players fight other Pokémon while obtaining items and finding stairs to the next floor, exiting the dungeon after a fixed number of floors.
romajiTitle: pokemon mystery dungeon rescue team dx

title: ポケットモンスター ソード・シールド
difficultyExplanation: Excellent and very easy to follow for the most part. Despite being RPGs, the story is very linear and even if you end up not understanding some plot points, you will almost never be “stuck” on a puzzle or not knowing where to go.
description: The first real mainline Pokémon game on Switch, not much to say. Play it if you like Pokémon.

title: ポケットモンスター スカーレット・バイオレット
difficultyExplanation: Average pokémon game with the usual RPG terminology but no really difficult vocab. Has furigana support so maybe slightly easier if you can't hook.
description: Pokémon Scarlet & Violet, standard pokémon gameplay.

title: ぼくの夏休み
difficultyExplanation: Main character is a child and everyone talks to him accordingly, very rarely going into more complex sentences and with reasonable speaking pace (game is fully voiced). That being said, the dialogue advances automatically and there's no furigana.
description: Boku's parents take him to spend his summer vacation with at his aunt and uncle's house. You have complete freedom as the player to choose how he'll spend it. Probably one of the most relaxing and immersive games you'll ever play.

title: ときめきメモリアル
difficultyExplanation: Everyday slice of life dialogue, conversations are mostly short and easy to follow, game is fully voiced, no furigana.
description: The dating sim to end all dating sims. Relive highschool all over again all over again in a game that objectifies love in the best possible way.

title: ときめきメモリアル2
difficultyExplanation: Similar to the first game above. It has more features such as honorifics being used to address certain girls, a weather system, more events and QoL features. Recommended to play this one over the other one if you want to get into this series.
description: See above.

title: Filsnown ～光と刻～
difficultyExplanation: Vocab is primarily easy fantasy JRPG fare with some brief spikes in difficulty when talking to gods. Both menu and dialogue text can be parsed easily with texthooking (see Neko Project II).
description: Long time ago, seven gods who were guarding the Earth defeated the evil god Gadim. But time has passed, and the seven benevolent gods have vanished one by one. Evil has awaken from its slumber. It's time for somebody else - a human - to become a hero and to defeat it once and for all. This chosen one is a young girl named Thiria Fray. She must find other girls with supernatural powers to aid her on her quest to defeat the evil.

title: Final Fantasy III (PSP 3D Remake)
difficultyExplanation: The story is simple, the plot is straightforward and the dialogues short and straight to the point. Most of the RPG vocabulary is in katakana so it would not be too difficult to lookup. Besides, it's a nice entry point to FF series.
description: With the power of light nearly eclipsed by the power of darkness, only the crystals' four chosen adventurers can save the world.

title: Tail Concerto
difficultyExplanation: It has simple everyday language with adventure bits. It mostly consists of dialogues between characters. Dialogues progress only after a button press, so there is almost always plenty of time to read it. It doesn't have furigana, but all the main story dialogues are voiced. The only difficult part is the animated cutscenes which lack subtitles.
description: It is an adventure platformer about anthropomorphic cats and dogs for PS1. The game looks like a shonen anime with a kind dog-policeman as a protagonist and a trio of cat-girls as baddies. The player must take control of a police robo and stop the mischievous Black Cats Gang. The game itself is short and can be completed in 4-6 hours.

title: Final Fantasy VII
difficultyExplanation: Some special words here and there, but total amount of unique words is no more than 5000ish, so it's very doable for someone who knows a fraction of that.
description: The game's story follows Cloud Strife, a mercenary who joins an eco-terrorist organization to stop a world-controlling megacorporation from using the planet's life essence as an energy source. Events send Cloud and his allies in pursuit of Sephiroth, a former member of the corporation who seeks to destroy the planet.

title: KIGEN 輝きの覇者
difficultyExplanation: Vocab primarily focuses on jrpg fantasy terms with some sci-fi terminology. Battles are real time with a variety of different skills (so a little tricky to read if you’re a slow reader) but nothing too difficult. Some uncommon vocabulary but can be quickly parsed via texthooking (see Neko Project II).
description: Shizuni is a planet in the solar system of the star Vanas. The humans have built a civilization there, similar to medieval Europe of our Earth. Whenever forces of darkness threaten the planet, it releases three shining orbs. These orbs choose their heroes, who would then join forces and defeat the evil. This time around, one of such heroes is Kanan, a young knight who has swore to serve his king. He must find the other heroes and save the planet, before it is once again controlled by the dark forces.

title: エストポリス伝記II
difficultyExplanation: Standard fantasy JRPG vocabulary but because it’s on the SNES not as much kanji usage as you’d hope and some things are very pixelated making it more difficult than it really is.
description: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals is a prequel to Lufia & the Fortress of Doom. Its events take place ninety-nine years prior to it, and it explains the origin of the series' antagonists, the group of super-humans known as the Sinistrals. The player controls the ancestor of the first game's protagonist, the swordsman Maxim. After having encountered a mysterious woman named Iris, Maxim goes on a journey to find other heroes who would help him to stop the Sinistrals from destroying the world.
romajiTitle: lufia ii rise of the sinistrals

title: ファイナルファンタジーX
difficultyExplanation: The game itself is not necessarily easy but the language I found surprisingly straightforward. Maybe the easiest FF language wise.
description: The game's story revolves around a group of adventurers and their quest to defeat a rampaging monster known as Sin. The player character is Tidus, a star athlete in the fictional sport of blitzball, who finds himself in Spira after Sin attacked his home city of Zanarkand.

title: ラングリッサー ドラマティックエディション
difficultyExplanation: The in-game dialogue is easy and voiced but some characters could be be difficult to understand due to Keigo. The pre-mission exposition is full of uncommon war terms and vocab-wise rings pretty close to other fantasy SRPGS like Fire Emblem. Cutscenes are voiced but have no subtitles and would be difficult for an early learner.
description: This is a remake of two games: Langrisser (known as Warsong in the USA) and its sequel, Langrisser II – or, better to say, the enhanced version of this sequel, known as Der Langrisser.

title: Chrono Trigger
difficultyExplanation: Pretty straightforward plot, general fantasy setting and vocabulary. The dialogues are pretty straightforward with an easy-to-follow story.
description: When a new invention malfunctions, MC and his friends end up in the past and need to find a way back to the present. Epic JRPG stuff ensues.

title: The Sims 3
difficultyExplanation: The Sims 3 is chock full of day-to-day life language, which can be incredibly helpful for building up practical vocabulary, in pure-reading format - so as long as the player makes an active effort to read through any text that crops up, and doesn't ignore it. Sentences and paragraphs aren't too long, so despite the variety of topics that are in the game, it can be easier to read. The game is technically hookable, but is probably easier to play using YomiNinja.
description: Create the lives you've always wanted! Ready to live a freer, more creative life? In The Sims™ 3, you can let your fantasies run wild as you design your ideal world. Start with your Sim, refining each shape, color and personality trait until you get the precise person that pleases you. Design your dream home, but don’t let a grid limit you; place, rotate and stack furniture and walls freely and to your heart’s content.

title: Voice of Cards ドラゴンの島
difficultyExplanation: Tabletop-like game which works in a turn-based system making it easier for Japanese learners because they don't have to rush to understand what's going on. It is 100% voiced. It's a series so you can enjoy the other games too.
description: On the Isle of Bliss, a Dragon said to bring catastrophe in its wake arrives. Queen Nilla sends adventurer bands to slay the Dragon and the monsters that emerged in its wake. Adventurer Ash and his monster partner Mar takes on the job for coin, being joined by the witch Melanie as she also seeks the Dragon. They often cross paths and are impeded by Wynifred and Sherwyn of the Ivory Order, a group who control a panacea called Dragontears.
romajiTitle: voice of cards the isle dragon roars

title: WitchSpring R
difficultyExplanation: Fantasy vocabulary and lots of menu popups with descriptions but the characters all use really simple grammar and the menus are really easy to read (no insane lingo) and whitenoisable, so you can just focus on dialogue and pick the easiest gameplay difficulty.
description: WitchSpring R is a story-driven RPG with a unique gaming system blending elements of simulation, item collection, and adventure. Discover the perfect combination of fairytale-like graphics and deep worldbuilding! Accompany Pieberry, a young witch running from a Witch Hunt, as she embarks on a grand adventure!

title: ファイアーエムブレム エンゲージ
difficultyExplanation: The game has the obvious fantasy vocabulary, which makes the entry a little difficult. However, this specific vocabulary is frequently repeated. There is no furigana, but the game is almost completely voiced except for the menus and tutorial texts. Knowledge from previous games is not needed but makes for a better experience.
description: After sleeping for 1000 years, the divine dragon Alear awakens and has to collect all emblem rings to fight the fell dragon together with the help of their friends.

title: MONSTER HUNTER RISE
difficultyExplanation: Has a lot of difficult and made-up words but isn't very dialogue heavy.
description: As with previous Monster Hunter titles, Monster Hunter Rise has the player take the role of a Hunter, tasked with slaying or capturing large monsters using a variety of weapons, tools, and environmental features to damage and weaken them while surviving their attacks.

title: Persona 4
difficultyExplanation: A lot of everyday language with some non-trivial bits thrown in due to the nature of mystery games. Dialogue is pretty regular overall.
description: The story revolves around Yu Narukami, a young teenager who moves to the town of Inaba, where a mysterious string of murders is taking place. Upon discovering a distorted TV World and acquiring a mysterious power known as "Persona", Yu and his friends decide to investigate the murders and save others from being killed.

title: Persona 5
difficultyExplanation: Same as above, pretty okay with some mystery game vocabulary.
description: Persona 5 is a game about the internal and external conflicts of a group of troubled high school students – the protagonist and a collection of compatriots he meets in the game's story – who live dual lives as Phantom Thieves.

title: ASTLIBRA Revision
difficultyExplanation: Language used by the main cast is mostly simple, but no voice acting makes it a bit less accessible. Some parts are a big jump in difficulty, especially in the later chapters of the story.
description: 2D action RPG that's incredibly fun, with satisfying gameplay and fun RPG elements. Lots of text. The action and story parts are divided well, so it's a very good mix of reading and gameplay. Early 2000's RPG vibes.

title: 英雄伝説VI 空の軌跡
difficultyExplanation: Lots of dialogue, lots of NPC, story is not super easy but it's still manageable.
description: The first trilogy in the Trails of series (sixth overall in the Legend of Heroes series.) The game follows protagonists Estelle Bright and her adopted brother Joshua, who journey through the country of Liberl to train to become senior Bracers, members of a non-government multinational organization that acts to keep the peace and protect civilians. You should play all three games, this is the description of the first one.
romajiTitle: the legend of heroes trails in the sky

title: 英雄伝説 零の軌跡・碧の軌跡
difficultyExplanation: More or less the same as sky but it starts getting more complicated topics later on, still relatively manageable though. I recommend playing these after you've played the sky trilogy so you should already be experienced enough (and the story will make sense more sense.)
description: Sequel to the above made in a dual edition. The protagonist, Lloyd Bannings, is a rookie police detective. At the beginning of Zero, he is assigned to the Special Support Section (SSS), an odd-jobs branch of the city's police department, together with Elie MacDowell, heiress to a political dynasty, Randolph "Randy" Orlando, a laid-back ex-soldier, and Tio Plato, a young girl and electronics genius.
romajiTitle: the legend of heroes trails from zero

title: コープスパーティ
difficultyExplanation: The game is extremely gripping so the difficulty isn't really an issue if you have a basic level of Japanese literacy.
description: The plot of the original Corpse Party game concerns a group of Japanese high school students, celebrating their school's culture festival. The group are telling ghost stories when a sudden earthquake transports them to a dilapidated schoolhouse in an alternate dimension. The school is haunted by the ghosts of people who have been trapped there.

title: 那由多の軌跡
difficultyExplanation: The name mentions it's a Kiseki/Trails game, however it's more like a spin-off/side story and can be played without having played any other kiseki game. The language is not particularly hard and it's not very text heavy. For most of the game you just have to go through various stages and fight enemies, and there are clear quest markers on the stage selection telling you where to go even if you can't follow the story. The dialogues sometimes throw at you some tricky words, but overall it's pretty average for a JRPG.
description: The Legend of Nayuta is set in two worlds: the main characters' home world, and a mysterious world called Lost Heaven. The main characters' hometown is Remnant Island, located in the center of Ciencia Sea, a vast ocean with countless islands. Shooting stars have been continually falling from the sky for some time, leaving much of these piled up on the island. Stones known as "Star Fragments" have been discovered in these areas. By shining a light on them in a certain way, people can see the phantom world of Lost Heaven.

title: Judgment
difficultyExplanation: Not as hard as an average light novel or visual novel but there will still be some words that are not as common in normal conversation/easier media.
description: The game follows private detective Takayuki Yagami as he investigates a serial murder case in Kamurocho, a fictional district of Tokyo, Japan, previously featured in the Yakuza franchise.

title: 龍が如く0 誓いの場所
difficultyExplanation: The game takes place in showa era with a lot of yakuza speech, and especially if it's the first one in the series for you then you'll not be used to the language. The interface makes use of a lot of kanji (it gives Showa vibes) and also a significant portion of the game takes place in Osaka so you have a lot of kansai slang as one of the main characters speaks kansai.
description: Yakuza 0 takes place in late 1988, during the bubble era of Japan, in which real estate and stock market prices were greatly inflated. The two central protagonists of the game are Kazuma Kiryu, a junior Tojo Clan yakuza in Kamurochō who is forced out of the clan due to a murder accusation, and Goro Majima, a disgraced former Tojo Clan yakuza who works as a cabaret manager in Sotenbori to earn his way back into the clan.

title: 龍が如く 極
difficultyExplanation: Easier than Yakuza 0 as there's less kansai, although the yakuza slang is still quite present. A lot of the side quests aren't voiced and there's a lot of content to read and go through. I would recommend reading Yakuza 0 first anyway.
description: Remake of the first Yakuza game on PS2. Like the original PlayStation 2 game, Yakuza Kiwami explores the life of a man named Kazuma Kiryu who is demoted from his clan after taking the blame for his boss's murder. After a decade in prison, Kiryu searches for his old friends who have gone missing.

title: 龍が如く 極2
difficultyExplanation: See above, it's the sequel and the same difficulty warnings apply.
description: Remake of the second Yakuza game on PS2. A year after leaving his former life in the Tojo Clan behind, ex-yakuza Kazuma Kiryu (Takaya Kuroda) is called back into action when the clan's Fifth Chairman, Yukio Terada (Kenji Nomura), is murdered by assassins from a rival organization, the Omi Alliance.

title: ファイナルファンタジーXIV
difficultyExplanation: Some difficult vocabulary from time to time, very long game with a lot of fantasy elements (duh). There are many different kinds of enemies that speak in different ways so it's medium-hard to hard depending.
description: Three nations try to recover after a world disaster as a foreign power tries to take over by using ancient magic. You are the Warrior of Light, capable of seeing the past in visions. Starting in one of the main nations, you will have to confront the foreign power and try to save the world.

title: 天穂のサクナヒメ
difficultyExplanation: Action RPG with rice farming as a big gameplay element. It has a lot of rice farming terminology and also some japanese mythology terminology and slight samurai speech and dialects.
description: Players control the goddess Princess Sakuna, who is tasked with exploring the Isle of Demons and clearing it of monsters while also looking after a small group of human characters. The game is split between two separate gameplay styles: side scrolling hack and slash platforming levels that are gradually revealed on a map of the island as players complete objectives, and a farming simulator where the player must grow rice in a small paddy in the hamlet where Sakuna and the humans live.

title: 真・女神転生V
difficultyExplanation: Has some challenging dialogue now and then but overall isn't too bad especially considering gameplay is the focus.
description: The protagonist, an ordinary high-school student, and his school friends Yuzuru Atsuta and Ichiro Dazai are caught up in a mysterious earthquake and transported to Da'at; an alternative apocalyptic version of Tokyo amidst an almighty battle between angels and demons. As he travels in this world, he shortly becomes overrun by demons and is nearly killed, only to be saved by a god-like being, Aogami.

title: 真・女神転生III NOCTURNE
difficultyExplanation: Some challenging dialogue now and again due to deities being the focus of the game series, but otherwise standard JRPG language.
description: Nocturne follows a high school student in post-apocalyptic Tokyo, who is transformed into the demonic Demi-fiend after the world undergoes Conception, an apocalyptic event triggered by a sinister cult to enable the world's rebirth in a new form.

title: Elden Ring
difficultyExplanation: Has hard dialogue for a JRPG and a lot of made-up words.
description: You play as the Tarnished, as you journey through The Lands Between, face the demigods, and try to understand the machinations of cosmic forces beyond your control.

title: ゼルダの伝説 ブレス オブ ザ ワイルド
difficultyExplanation: There is some more complicated vocabulary along with made-up words, but you can still enjoy the story to its fullest by ignoring a good deal of the details.
description: The first entry on the Switch of the world-famous Legend of Zelda entry. Once again you'll need to face Ganondorf to save the princess Zelda.
romajiTitle: the legend of zelda breath of the wild

title: ゼルダの伝説 ティアーズ オブ ザ キングダム
difficultyExplanation: The sequel of the game above, most things said above apply there too.
description: The second entry on the Switch of Legend of Zelda and the sequel to the game above. The plot is similar once again, with the same freedom to do whatever you want but on steroids.
romajiTitle: the legend of zelda tears of the kingdom

title: ファイアーエムブレム 風花雪月
difficultyExplanation: Lots of medieval vocabulary but the dialogue usually isn't too bad. The story is a bit hard to grasp depending on which route you go through first and you'll need to follow to plot to understand what's going on.
description: Three Houses is set on the continent of Fódlan, divided between three ruling powers currently at peace. These nations are connected through the Garreg Mach Monastery, which houses a church and an officer's school for students from each nation. Taking the role of Byleth, a former mercenary with a mysterious past and the academy's newest professor, the player must choose a class to lead and guide their students through a series of battles.

title: MOTHER2 ギーグの逆襲
difficultyExplanation: Surreal themes and story with lots of weird use of vocabulary and syntax. It is a bit hard to follow at times with fantasy vocabulary. Sometimes parodies elements of other JRPGs.
description: Mother 2, known as EarthBound in the West takes place in the 1990s, several years after the events of Mother, in the fictional country of Eagleland, a parody of the United States. The player starts as a young boy named Ness as he investigates a nearby meteorite crash with his neighbor, Pokey, to find his neighbor's brother Picky. They find that an alien force, Giygas, has enveloped and consumed the world in hatred and consequently turned animals, humans, and objects into malicious creatures.

title: Mass Effect Series
difficultyExplanation: It's fantastic pure-reading immersion if the player can commit to that, but contains a lot of political and technological language, as well as terms specific to the game/world, which makes it challenging. Being able to hear the dialogue in English may help with comprehension when reading through the text in Japanese, however. With how dialogue-heavy the game is, it plays like a VN or Persona, with a shooter aspect - across three 25+ hour games
description: One person is all that stands between humanity and the greatest threat it’s ever faced. Relive the legend of Commander Shepard in the highly acclaimed Mass Effect trilogy. Your choices seamlessly travel from one game to the next. Each decision you make will control the outcome of every mission, every relationship, every battle — and even the fate of the galaxy itself.

title: ファイナルファンタジーXVI
difficultyExplanation: Lack of texthooking, all dialogue is real time (no log, no pausing), the English version of the game is not closely translated from Japanese so you can't easily compare versions, lots of less common kanji and terminology being used all make this game significantly hard. It's probably the hardest FF game language-wise.
description: Final Fantasy XVI is set in the twin continents of Valisthea, currently divided between six nations who hold power through access to magical Crystals and Dominants, humans who act as hosts for each nation's Eikon. Tensions between the nations escalate as a magical drought dubbed the Blight begins consuming the land.

title: うたわれるもの 散りゆく者への子守唄
difficultyExplanation: The language is full of made up words, often with very long and confusing katakana strings. It uses a lot of non-standard/unusual kanji, it does provide furigana for a lot of those words but often the furigana doesn't match what the word actually is and sometimes uses very archaic language and every character has their own speech quirks and dialectal/slang way of speaking (often very archaic).
description: Utawarerumono is a story centering around the masked protagonist, Hakuowlo, who one day is found by a family of two girls and their grandmother in a nearby forest close to their village. He is badly injured and is soon found to have amnesia, so they take him to their home and treat him until he is well again. Hakuowlo is soon accepted into their village where he stays and lives with them, but before long Hakuowlo finds that life in this village is being oppressed by the greedy ruler of the land their village resides in.

title: 英雄伝説 閃の軌跡
difficultyExplanation: Cold steel 1 is very straightforward and not too political but Cold Steel 2 starts getting more political later on. These two rank at Medium-Hard. In comparison, Cold Steel 3 and 4 are a bump in difficulty. They contain significantly more dialogue and side content (often unvoiced) and the themes are very political with lots of complex topics.
description: A tetralogy, the sequel to the Trails of Zero/Azure games.
romajiTitle: the legend of heroes trails of cold steel

title: 原神
difficultyExplanation: A lot of chinese/rare kanji, dense writing, so much text to read especially in world quests. Lots of rare words, made up words that natives have difficulty reading. Sheer volume of text will make you better at reading.
description: Genshin Impact is a massive game that throws players into a world where the Archons rule over the land, and elemental visions are granted to worthy mortals. The game follows the Traveler as they go on a quest to find their missing sibling with the companion Paimon. Gacha game.

title: アニマルズ
difficultyExplanation: Honestly, nothing really difficult to see here. There might be some fashion or work lingo, but it's very approachable for beginners.
description: Shikamori Umi is an overwhelmed office worker. She doesn't like herself and what she has become while working in the office, and instead of returning and remaining the same, she tries her luck in a makeup agency called Animal Beauty. With her new mindset she becomes an intern, where she meets Kazao, a photographer who becomes her friend, and Sakaki Keisuke, the handsome CEO of Animal Beauty.

title: ユニコーンに乗って
difficultyExplanation: Same as above, the only difficulty is some office lingo here and there but the rest is easy.
description: When Sana Narukawa was only 23-years-old, she co-founded startup company Dream Pony. Her dream was to have people all over the world use her app. Now, Sana Narukawa is 26-years-old. Her company is in its 3rd year of existence. The company grew rapidly initially, but is now experiencing a decline in its growth. Due to the slowdown, Sana Narukawa feels nervous everyday. In her personal life, she has feelings for Ko Suzaki, who is a co-founder of Dream Pony.

title: 今際の国のアリス
difficultyExplanation: Straightforward action-focused story with Battle Royale themes and tropes. No special vocabulary needed. Difficulty ramps up slightly only when each game's rules are being explained, but even if you don't understand the spoken explanation fully at first, once the game starts the visuals should fill in the gaps. Possibly ideal for beginners.
description: In Tokyo, video-game-obsessed Arisu hangs out with his friends Chōta and Karube. After causing an altercation in Shibuya Crossing, the trio hide from police in the station bathroom but reemerge to find the city empty. At night, they follow a billboard's instructions to a "game arena". There, the group is joined by a high school girl and another woman, who informs them that once a player enters an arena, they cannot leave, as a laser will shoot them dead if they try.

title: 結婚できない男
difficultyExplanation: Nothing much to say, some architecture words from time to time.
description: Shinsuke Kuwano, a successful architect at 40, enjoys living by himself. He doesn't like people but somehow is able to design wonderful houses for them. Kuwano is incredibly socially awkward, to the point of being rude, however, he often means well, and is generally at a loss as to why he annoys people around him (which he does consistently). While he is a loner, he has regular contact with his family, his mother in particular is trying to get him married.

title: House
difficultyExplanation: Mostly day-to-day conversations making it somewhat easy.
description: Hoping to find a sense of connection to her late mother, Gorgeous takes a trip to the country to visit her aunt at their ancestral house. She invites her six friends, Prof, Melody, Mac, Fantasy, Kung Fu, and Sweet, to join her. The girls soon discover that there is more to the old house than meets the eye.

title: 持続可能な恋ですか？～父と娘の結婚行進曲～
difficultyExplanation: The main character's father writes entries for a dictionary and sometimes waxes philosophical, but otherwise pretty simple.
description: Sawada Kyoka gets into arguments with her father Sawada Rintaro constantly and she is also burdened with taking care of him. One day, Sawada Rintaro finds a divorce document among his late wife's belongings. This pushes Sawada Rintaro into wanting to remarry. He also pushes his daughter Sawada Kyoka to find a marriage partner.
romajiTitle: jizoku kanona koidesu ka chichitoko no kekkon koshinkyoku

title: 着飾る恋には理由があって
difficultyExplanation: Not much to say, easy vocabulary nothing too hard here.
description: Kurumi, a publicist for an interior design company is so busy with work she forgets to renew her apartment lease, so her friend Koko helps her find a new place, but it's a share house with three strangers. Though their personalities clash, Kurumi falls in love, deepens her friendships, and learns to take off her "armor" and live as herself.
romajiTitle: kikazaru koi niha riyuu ga atte

title: 流れ星
difficultyExplanation: Good for learning short and simple conversations. There are some minor instances of rakugo but skipping through them will not have any impact on how well you comprehend the plot.
description: Takenouchi plays an aquarium employee named Kengo, who seems ordinary at first glance but actually possesses a secret that he would sacrifice everything in order to protect. Meanwhile, Ueto plays Risa, a young woman working in the sex trade in order to pay off her brother's debt, though her situation has led her to contemplate suicide. These two characters, both full of despair, meet each other and end up entering a contract marriage purely for its benefits.

title: あなたの番です
difficultyExplanation: No complicated language, has a lot of repeating words/phrases.
description: Nana and Shota are a newlywed couple, and Nana is 15 years older than Shota. After they move in a new apartment, Nana and Shota become involved in murder cases that take place at the apartment. Residents get murdered one by one. Some residents have a motive, but those suspects have an alibi. Because of this, an arrest has yet to be made.

title: 姉ちゃんの恋人
difficultyExplanation: Everyday language, nothing too hard.
description: When Momoko Adachi was in high school, her parents died in an accident. She was left with her 3 younger siblings. To support her family, Momoko Adachi gave up on going to a university and picked up a job at a hardware store. 9 years later, she is now 27-years-old. Her 3 younger siblings are 20, 17, and 14-years-old. Momoko Adachi places her sibling's happiness before anything else. One day, she meets Yoshioka-san at work. She is attracted to Yoshioka-san, who smiles all the time, but he has a secret.

title: 坂の途中の家
difficultyExplanation: Common everyday language with a few legal terms popping up now and again.
description: Yamazaki Risako lives with her husband Yoichiro and 3-year-old daughter Fumika. One day, she receives a notification from the court that she has been selected as an alternate member of the jury for a shocking criminal case. The defendant is on trial for causing the death of her 8-month-old daughter by dropping her into the bathtub.

title: インフルエンス
difficultyExplanation: Pretty much only everyday language, nothing too hard.
description: Yuri goes to a female novelist and tells her that she and two of her friends committed three murders. Yuri asks the novelist to write a story about them.

title: Battle Royale
difficultyExplanation: The main characters are teenagers in a survival situation, so the language is not terribly complex. The explanation of the game's rules is lengthy and must be understood. One major character speaks in decently thick Kansai-ben. Takeshi Kitano is mumbly (maybe that's just my opinion).
description: In a dystopian Japan wishing to cut down on teenage delinquency, a high school class find themselves kidnapped and brought to an abandoned island, where they are to fight each other to the death until only one remains.

title: 不幸くんはキスするしかない!
difficultyExplanation: Standard romance drama, subs are available which makes it easier.
description: Fukuhara Kota is a university student who has unnaturally bad luck and after kissing Shinomiya Naoya, a good-looking fellow student with supernatural good luck, he asks him to be come friends. But Shinomiya Naoya misunderstands the suggestion as a request of dating!
romajiTitle: fukou kun wa kiss suru shikanai

title: 消えた初恋
difficultyExplanation: Your average high school romance drama in terms of difficulty, so definitely approachable.
description: Aoki has a crush on the girl in the seat next to him in class but after an incident Ida, another classmate, starts to think that Aoki has a crush on him!

title: チャンネルはそのまま！
difficultyExplanation: There is some TV and reporting lingo but it's not too hard. The main character can sometimes talk a bit fast or be over the top (or just plain stupid), but outside of that it's easy.
description: Meet Yukimaru Hanako, a 22-year-old and fresh young reporter from Hokkaido. She's just been hired by a local television station to do field reporting, and we are here to watch the launching of her career!

title: ヒルナンデス！
difficultyExplanation: Standard Japanese, there are some subtitles. Some accents when the hosts talk to people in other parts of the country but should be manageable.
description: This show gives profitable, interesting and practical information on delicacies, fashion, popular places. The show featured a series of regular members who only appeared on a particular day of the week. These regular members were changed periodically.

title: 誰も知らない
difficultyExplanation: Coming of age story, mostly kids and teens talking.
description: In a small Tokyo apartment, twelve-year-old Akira must care for his younger siblings after their mother leaves them and shows no sign of returning.

title: ブラッシュアップライフ
difficultyExplanation: Mostly slice of life vocab with a bunch of work-related jargon here and there.
description: A comedy focusing on Kondo Asami, a 33-year-old single woman who lives with her parents and works at the local city hall, and suddenly finds herself starting her life over from scratch. It happens out of a sudden and Asami finds herself on a bed in an obstetrics and gynecology clinic, where she meets her young parents and begins her life all over again.

title: バッシング
difficultyExplanation: The vocabulary is pretty standard but you need to pay attention to pick up what is happening since it doesn't exactly throw the whole plot at your face. Still, it's decently easy.
description: Yuko is a Japanese girl who was taken hostage in Iraq while volunteering there as an aid worker. Finally released and back in her hometown, Yuko finds herself ostracized as a national disgrace by society that sees her helping a country other than Japan, and the embarrassment of getting captured but not killed, as things of which to be brutally ashamed.

title: 逃げるは恥だが役に立つ
difficultyExplanation: Mostly everyday language but has some more difficult bits from time to time.
description: 25-year-old Moriyama Mikuri graduated but had no job offers. She became a temporary employee but was even laid off. So while she is taking a break right now, Mikuri feels unwanted and displaced. She starts work as a housekeeper for bachelor Tsuzaki Hiramasa by chance. One day, he proposes a contract marriage to her. The two of them get married in secret, but will their married life work out?
romajiTitle: nigeru wa haji da ga yaku ni tatsu

title: マイ★ボス マイ★ヒーロー
difficultyExplanation: Mostly average high school content, not too difficult and easy even without subs. That being said, sometimes characters are speaking like Yakuza and it can be troublesome to understand what they say.
description: The show is about Makio Sakaki, also known as "Tornado", a 27-year-old yakuza, who wants to succeed his father at the head of the gang. But Makio is a little dumb, so his father decides to send him back to high school and makes a deal with him: if he can graduate he can become the new leader of the gang. If Makio doesn't graduate, the position of boss will be given to his younger brother, Mikio.

title: 発見！タカトシランド
difficultyExplanation: Nicely paced show where the two hosts visit various places in Hokkaido with guests, usually with good food.
description: The dialogue isn't too hard, the subtitles help quite a bit. Since a lot of episodes center on places to eat, even a beginner can understand what's going on.

title: 乃木坂工事中
difficultyExplanation: The difficulty depends on the specific episode, but it usually isn't too hard since the Nogizaka members speak clearly with good 標準語 (standard Japanese) accent.
description: Nogizaka46 variety show hosted by the comedy duo Bananaman. Each episode discusses a different topic with the various members of Nogizaka46 doing or discussing something.

title: 日向坂出会いましょう
difficultyExplanation: On-screen captions are usually available, making it easier for the viewer to follow. The difficulty also varies on the topic of the specific episode but I believe it is relatively easier than Nogizaka Under Construction because it is easier to understand the hosts in this show.
description: Similar style to Nogizaka Under Construction but starring Hinatazaka members instead and also hosted by comedy duo Audrey.

title: カルテット
difficultyExplanation: Nothing too difficult here, although there are references to pop culture. Overall alright for a beginner but they might speak a bit fast, using subs is highly recommended.
description: Maki Maki, Sebuki Suzume, Beppu Tsukasa, and Iemori Yutaka happen to meet and form a quartet. They even begin to live together in Karuizawa during the winter, but there is a big hidden secret.

title: 仄暗い水の底から
difficultyExplanation: Fairly easy movie with Japanese subtitles available online. Most of the story is told visually so even if you don't understand the dialogue you can understand what is happening.
description: The plot follows a divorced mother who moves into a rundown apartment with her daughter, and experiences supernatural occurrences including a mysterious water leak from the floor above.

title: ベイビーわるきゅーれ
difficultyExplanation: A reasonable amount of slang and some macho yakuza-style talk, but nothing too difficult.
description: Teenage girls Chisato and Mahiro are highly skilled assassins, though they find working part-time jobs and sharing a Tokyo apartment to be as difficult as any of their hits. When their actions anger the yakuza, they must overcome the strains in their friendship and fight together.

title: １リットルの涙
difficultyExplanation: The main difficulty is the medical vocabulary from time to time but overall alright.
description: Aya, a high school aged girl and the oldest daughter of her family who run a tofu shop starts to fall down often and has random bouts of confusion. Based on a true story. This is the saddest thing I've ever seen.

title: 美しい彼
difficultyExplanation: Part of the difficulty is that not everything is explicitly stated. They tend to speak quite fast. That being said, the plot isn't the worst to understand.
description: Seventeen-year-old Hira, who is at the bottom of the class, tries to remain invisible at school, never wanting to open his mouth and expose his stuttering speech to his classmates. He views the world through his camera lens, detached until one day, Kiyoi Sou walks through the classroom door. The impact is instantaneous.

title: A.K.A. Serial Killer
difficultyExplanation: The narrator is constantly speaking about the various murders in the movie so you need to pay attention in order not to lose track.
description: AKA Serial Killer documents the social upheaval and political oppression that roiled Japan in the 1960s, profiling a nineteen-year-old serial killer Norio Nagayama. An indictment of media sensationalism, the film humanizes the young man by situating his crimes in the larger context of his environment.

title: United Red Army
difficultyExplanation: The movie being divided into multiple acts, you can understand an act even if you didn't understand the previous one which makes it slightly easier than usual movies where you need to grasp everything.
description: A film in three acts, discussing the 60s and 70s student movements in Japan using archive footage and a narrator.

title: 殺し屋１
difficultyExplanation: Extreme gorefest and lots of blood but nothing too crazy to understand.
description: As sadomasochistic yakuza enforcer Kakihara searches for his missing boss he comes across Ichi, a repressed and psychotic killer who may be able to inflict levels of pain that Kakihara has only dreamed of.

title: 逆噴射家族
difficultyExplanation: The dialogue in the movie isn't that complicated but a downside is the audio.
description: Classic "family" genre movie. A family of 4 moves into a new place but the grandpa decides to come too and the family has to adapt, etc.

title: 愛のむきだし
difficultyExplanation: Great story and great comedy, pretty long though. You need to pay proper attention throughout so it's a bit harder.
description: The story of a teenage boy named Yu, who falls for Yoko, a girl he runs into while working as an “up-skirt” photographer in an offshoot of the porn industry.

title: 池袋ウエストゲートパーク
difficultyExplanation: Has some detective vocabulary but overall decently easy, although there are some yankees in the movie which makes it slightly harder to understand.
description: This story follows a young man named Makoto, who lives in Ikebukuro West Gate Park, an area known for youth delinquency and gangs. In fact, one of Makoto's best friends from high school, Takeshi, is the "king" or leader, of one such gang, called the G-Boys.

title: ハコヅメ～交番女子の逆襲～
difficultyExplanation: Has a bunch of police-related vocabulary.
description: Rookie police officer Mai is about to hand in her resignation when she meets 30-year-old Fuji Seiko, the former ace detective of the Criminal Investigations Division. Seiko is said to have been forced to transfer to the police box for harassing a subordinate at work but... This encounter between Mai and Seiko will significantly change their lives as they are suddenly paired up.

title: 恋せぬふたり
difficultyExplanation: It seems like SOL but some of the convos are about fairly abstract topics without many contextual clues.
description: Sakuko finds it difficult to live in a society which operates under the assumption that people will fall in love with each other. She meets supermarket employee Takahashi when she goes to support a "fall-in-love" campaign by her junior at work. She is startled when she hears him say that there are people who don't fall in love.

title: ハケンの品格
difficultyExplanation: It has some office lingo which is a great way to learn about work and company structures in japanese companies. Probably less difficult if you're a salaryman and are aware of corporate structuring.
description: Oomae Haruko is an A+ Temp worker who never cracks a smile, does not mince words, and leaves work at 5 o’clock on the dot. Her cynical nature indicates she has something painful to hide.
