Satonaka Kensuke has just been promoted to the head of S&F's new Marketing Division. Saddled with a rag-tag staff, he is struggling to lift his division off the ground. Placed in Kensuke's department, Oomae finds herself working harder than ever before.

title: ロングバケーション
difficultyExplanation: Standard drama, nothing stands out too much.
description: Sena is a college music graduate who dreams of becoming a professional musician and a world-class pianist. Minami is an out-of-work model. The two down-on-their-luck persons with very different personalities find themselves bonding over their similar situations in life.

title: ナンバMG5
difficultyExplanation: Has some yankee speak but other than that standard.
description: Born in a family of delinquents, Nanba Tsuyoshi is expected to succeed as the strongest delinquent in school. Unbeknownst to his family however, he decides to enroll in the top high school in town to live as a normal high schooler. Can he maintain his double life as the strongest delinquent in town and as a normal high schooler?

title: おかえりモネ
difficultyExplanation: Pretty long drama, has some work-related vocabulary. Some character have a regional accent. Other than this, quite easy to follow.
description: Momone Nagaura walks on a mountain with the weather forecaster. She hears from the weather forecaster that the weather forecaster can predict the future. Momone Nagaura becomes touched by that comment and decides to become a weather forecaster. In 2019, a major typhoon approaches Japan. To help her hometown, she heads to Kesennuma Bay.

title: 花咲舞が黙っていない！
difficultyExplanation: The main difficulty comes from the bank language and vocabulary, the rest is approachable.
description: Based on a book by the same author who wrote the books Hanzawa Naoki is based on (池井戸潤). While Hanzawa Naoki focuses on big financial corporate drama, this is more focused on day-to-day operations of banks. Very educational and fun. Not as serious or dramatic as Hanzawa Naoki.

title: 最愛
difficultyExplanation: Some characters speak in the Hida dialect. Also has some detective jargon.
description: A suspense love story centered around Sanada Rio, a businesswoman who suddenly became an important reference for a murder case; a detective who is Rio's first love and is trying to pursue the truth of the case; and a lawyer who wants to protect Rio by all means.

title: コールドケース ～真実の扉～
difficultyExplanation: Cop detective show with pretty standard jargon for the genre.
description: Yuri Ishikawa and her team try to crack unresolved cold cases in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan.

title: 地味にスゴイ! 校閲ガール
difficultyExplanation: Work/publishing industry-related and literary jargon. They explain the more specialized words and the rest is quite easy to follow other than a couple of puns here and there.
description: This charming work drama has plenty of light moments and lets us peek behind the curtain at the publishing industry. The main character has dreamt for years of becoming an editor for her favorite fashion magazine. She gets accepted into the publishing company but they send her to a basement office where she is asked to... proofread!?!?? Maybe it's more fun than it seems. Has some romance on the side but it's not the main focus.
romajiTitle: jimi ni sugoi koetsu garu kono etsuko

title: 勇者ヨシヒコと魔王シリーズ
difficultyExplanation: Has JRPG vocab and the jokes can be hard to catch.
description: A pure young man named Yoshihiko becomes chosen as a hero, and he sets out on a journey in order to save a village. This is more of a Dragon Quest and JRPG genre parody series.
romajiTitle: yuusha yoshihiko to maou no shiro

title: Good Luck!!
difficultyExplanation: Work and aviation-related jargon.
description: A light-hearted work drama set in the airline industry. The main character is a young first officer working towards becoming a captain. There is a bit of romance but the focus is more on work. Great regular cast including other pilots, very competent flight attendants, and repair crew.

title: 妖怪! 百鬼夜高等学校
difficultyExplanation: Highschool drama, but it has youkai vocabulary and no subs.
description: When the clock in the school building strikes midnight, the campus will become "a school for yokais" that cannot be seen with human eyes. Tanaka Kazuo is a human high school student with no friends who is bullied by his classmates. He feels miserable and lonely, believing that he doesn't belongs anywhere. However eveything changes when he discovers the existence of the yokai realm.

title: 回路
difficultyExplanation: A little abstract, you need to properly pay attention to what's going on.
description: In the immense city of Tokyo, the darkness of the afterlife lurks some of its inhabitants who are desperately trying to escape the sadness and isolation of the modern world.

title: BORDER
difficultyExplanation: Has policy and forensic jargon, making it harder than your average drama.
description: Ango Ishikawa is a detective with smarts and a keen sense of observation. He's in a great physical shape and also highly ambitious. Ango also only focuses on his work and his personal life is pretty much non-existent. One day, Ango is shot in the head by the killer who is lurking at the crime scene. Ango hovers between life and death. Since then Ango can see and talk with the dead.

title: BORDER: Shokuzai
difficultyExplanation: The sequel to the above.
description: See above.

title: コウノドリ
difficultyExplanation: Has a bunch of medical jargon.
description: The drama revolves around Kounotori Sakura, an Ob-Gyn doctor working at the Persona General Medical Centre who is also a gifted jazz pianist. His mother had died in childbirth, and he was brought up in an orphanage, which is what fueled his ambition to be an ob-gyn. He hopes to be able to deliver every baby to this world, congratulating them on the gift of life given to their little bodies.

title: 豚と軍艦
difficultyExplanation: Audio quality is pretty bad due to the age of the film, it also has some old words that make it hard.
description: In the city of Yokosuka, Kinta and his lover Haruko, both involved with yakuza, brave the post-occupation period with a goal to be together.

title: リーガル・ハイ
difficultyExplanation: Main character talks fast with plenty of law and technological terminology. Some references can go over your head if you don't know Japanese culture and media that well.
description: Attorney Komikado Kensuke loves money, prestige and women, but also has a 100% winning rate when it comes to his legal cases. Mayuzumi Machiko is a rookie attorney who holds a strong sense of justice and passionate about protecting the weak. The two attorneys constantly clash, but in the courtroom, they cooperate in fighting as one.

title: キュア
difficultyExplanation: Can get really hard sometimes mostly because of the obscurity the movie has, along with a lot of detective terminology.
description: Kenichi Takabe, a Tokyo Metropolitan Police detective, is involved in the investigation of a bizarre series of violent killings by seemingly random perpetrators. In each case the murderers have been caught close to the scene of the crime. Each one has mutilated his or her victim by carving a large "X" into the neck or chest of the deceased. Although all of the perpetrators readily confess and remember their deeds, none seems to have substantial motives or explanations for their actions. Takabe is at a loss for answers.

title: Hero
difficultyExplanation: Has law terminology with some fast speaking characters. The audio quality might not be crystal clear either which doesn't help, the show being a bit old at this point.
description: Kuryu Kohei is an unconventional prosecutor at the Josai branch of the Tokyo District Public Prosecutors Office. One day Kuryu is asked to take on a case which his colleague, Shibayama, prosecuted. The case looks simple with a confession by the accused, but the accused changes his plea at the first hearing and now claims his innocence.

title: 半沢直樹
difficultyExplanation: Business thriller with a lot of hard business and finance terminology. Some made up words here and there too.
description: An idealistic banker takes on corruption and wrongdoing at his large corporate bank. While forging ties with some unlikely allies, he must use his financial expertise, his instincts about human nature, and his skills of improvisation to try to stay one step ahead of his powerful enemies.

title: TRICK
difficultyExplanation: Detective/comedy show. A lot of the comedy requires good knowledge of Japanese culture and news. The show is somewhat old so the audio quality might be lacking too.
description: Although 23-year-old Yamada Naoko is a talented illusionist, she is continuously fired from jobs and constantly hounded by her landlady for the rent being late. She refuses to give up her unusual vocation as she wants to follow in the footsteps of her famous magician father who died when she was a child.

title: 羅生門
difficultyExplanation: As a period piece, there are many archaic terms and turns of phrase. The performances are extremely stylized, which can make comprehension difficult. As an older film, the audio quality is not to modern standards. However, the plot is very clear; you could get the gist even if you didn't understand a word being said.
description: In Heian period Japan, a samurai is found dead in a grove. A bandit, the samurai's wife, the dead samurai himself channeled through a medium, and a woodcutter each give accounts of the events surrounding the samurai's death, but the accounts each contradict one another.

title: 軍師官兵衛
difficultyExplanation: Tends to use "old-timey" speech patterns which takes some getting used to. Helps to have some knowledge of Sengoku-era history, or Wikipedia on hand. At 50 episodes, a bigger commitment than most other dramas but so worth it.
description: This NHK taiga drama is set during the Sengoku period and follows the life and times of Kuroda Kanbei, who served primarily as Hideyoshi's strategist (with some overlap with Oda Nobunaga and Tokugawa Ieyasu's careers). It is an engaging portrait that covers the big events of the time, with a good mix of strategizing, negotiating, war, politics, and family moments.

title: 絞死刑
difficultyExplanation: A lot of symbolism and rhetorical questions make this movie very hard to follow.
description: A Korean man is sentenced to death in Japan but survives his execution, sending the authorities into a panic about what to do next.

title: フェルミ研究所 FermiLab
description: They add voice over manga panels and make a video out of it. I'm not sure but I think the series that they do videos on are their own mangas.
exampleVideo: 【漫画】正直ダサいと思っていること【あるある/マンガ動画】

description: Japanese Olympic Weightlifter makes a lot of content breaking down lifts and videos on his training.

description: Videos on sports/climbing.

description: Guy fishes for weird sea creatures and eats them. He also has a playlist of survival on foraged/fished food, so if Bear Grylls style is your jam, this is your go-to.

exampleVideo: ラバーガール・・・「別れさせ屋」／『ラバーガール ソロライブ「キャット」』より

title: Fischer's
description: One of Japan's most popular YouTube channels. It's a group channel with 6 members which probably influenced most of the main trends on Japanese YouTube today, for example hard subtitles and sound effects. As you watch more of their channel, you will grow to learn all the members and probably like most of their videos. They do lots of variety.
exampleVideo: 【第１回】アラームをつくれ！ジリリリリリ王で神曲がうまれて大爆笑したwww

title: SAWAYAN
description: Two Ukranians born and raised in Japan. They are Japanese and Russian natives but all of their videos are done in Japanese. They also do lots of variety content like Fischer's and can sometimes be childish but it's just light hearted fun. They like doing lots of pranks on each other.
exampleVideo: 【突撃】減量を頑張っているヤンの目の前で朝からマック爆食いしてみたw w w

title: おろちんゆー
description: He has plenty of inside jokes and makes lots of videos with a friend called ペインさかいくん and they have hilarious chemistry. He fishes and eats bugs pretty much, while taking lots of inspiration from orochimaru from naruto, mainly in the form of his voice. Can't recommend to people who find bugs disgusting though. If you get invested like me, check out the second channel おろちんゆーの素揚げ.
exampleVideo: ドでかい虹鱒が美味すぎる

title: えばそん
description: Canadian guy raised in Japan, he is a Japanese native. He makes high effort skits with editing and scripts, where he asks his viewers for input. You'll see the comments from his viewers in the videos.
exampleVideo: 【大喜利】こんなかき氷は嫌だ

title: ANTI BCSC
description: Group of 5 dudes who go around on motorcycles. Their content is very funny as they crack jokes the entire time, and it's great seeing the Japanese scenery. They're from Okayama so they speak Kansai-ben, but they tone it down for the videos so it's not really that strong.
exampleVideo: 【イッキ見】下ネタ禁止‼︎敗者は罰ゲームの愛媛大洲総集編

title: グロディーTV
description: Guy born in the DRC in Africa, moved to Belgium for a few years, then raised in Japan. He is a Japanese native. He goes around at night in Shibuya and interviews people, leading to some really funny moments.

title: ジョシュアinロンドン☆

So he's a second generation white japanese guy. Anyways, he interviews other nihonsodachi people. Great to get perspective on what it is like for them.

title: QuizKnock

exampleVideo: 【ぼろ平屋DIY】#1 ルームツアー 激安ずたぼろ平屋内部公開

My favorite videos from him are the ones where he humorously changes/creates new kana and kanji in Japanese.

title: HikakinTV
description: Hikakin is the most popular YouTuber in Japan. He has been making videos for over a decade, usually VLOG type videos with silly humor.
exampleVideo: 20億円のヒカキン新居ハウスツアー！超巨大室内温水プール&庭付きの家

title: Japanese podcast for beginners (Nihongo con Teppei)
difficultyExplanation: The words are introduced carefully. Topics repeat a lot. Teppei may use a word in English per episode to clarify something that is hard to explain in Japanese. Slower pace of speech.
description: Bright man in his forties, perfect for a first podcast. Teppei often repeats himself to reformulate and explain the same though. Has great intuition about what's hard or easy in the language. Obviously learner-targeted.

title: Japanese with Shun
difficultyExplanation: Short episodes (~7-10min). Slow speaking with pauses, limited grammar and vocabulary used mainly from Genki I, new vocab at the end of episodes. The limited grammar and slow speaking is what makes this easy. Overall, perfect for a beginner.
description: Daily life and various topics. Shun is a backpacker who has traveled to places such as South America and New Zealand and talks about life from his perspective. He is also interested in weightlifting and is a Japanese teacher. He also has a YouTube channel.

title: Nihongo con Teppei Z
difficultyExplanation: The podcast is pretty accessible as it is targeted towards beginners trying to learn Japanese. The host speaks slowly and clearly, so it is good as a first podcast.
description: Podcast oriented at beginners in Japanese where multiple topics are discussed.

title: Japanese with Teppei and Noriko
difficultyExplanation: Short to very short episodes, recurring topics, slice of life, food and so on. More complicated words are explained.
description: Unscripted. Great podcast to listen in parallel with Teppei Z. Teppei and Noriko are only meeting when they record this podcast, so their conversation starts as something very shallow and go deeper on each episode. They don't speak slowly, but because of recurring topics, you will understand a lot after the first 100 episodes.

title: YUYUの日本語Podcast
difficultyExplanation: Japanese man living in Mexico who makes Japanese content for learners. As such, it is adapted even for beginners.
description: Includes random stuff usually related to his own experiences. He accepts requests for podcast topic. Also does live streams nowadays.

title: Let’s learn Japanese from small talk!
difficultyExplanation: Learner-targeted, unscripted, not adapted, but hard words are often explained or sometimes mentioned in English. There is also a vocabulary list available for each episode.
description: Two women, everyday and slice of life topics. Good introduction to realistic 会話 podcasts that are still guided a bit for learners.

title: ことのは日本語の会話のpodcast
difficultyExplanation: The topics are typically not too advanced, and the audio is clear. It's a tiny bit harder than easy due to the fact that there are two hosts speaking to one another, which can complexify things a bit. This podcast is nonetheless targeted at learners, so if a rarer word comes up, it is often explained in simple Japanese.
description: The hosts are two women in their high 20s maybe low 30s, one of them is married. Main topics include life in Japan, あるあるs and just general daily conversation. They occasionally talk about societal issues.

title: 4989 Utaco
difficultyExplanation: Probably one of the easiest podcasts intended for native speakers. The host, Utaco, speaks clearly. Having familiarity with the way things work in America (such as signing up for college classes or what it's like to go to the DMV) leads to a big boost in comprehension.
description: Utaco lives with her husband and cats in California and talks about her struggles and difficulties in daily life (where the name of the podcast comes from 4989=四苦八苦). She has various corners like "What I miss about Japan," "My favorite things," and talks about learning English, going to college, getting a job, making friends, tap dancing, moving to a new town, and cultural differences between the US and Japan. Transcript

title: シノブとナルミの毒舌アメリカンライフ
difficultyExplanation: It's 雑談 with two adult Japanese women who have experience living in the states. So it can get a little bilingual from time to time, but mostly Japanese, spoken by adults.
description: Two women, Narumi and Shinobu. They met in Houston and started a podcast there. They talk about normal life topics. Narumi relocated to Okinawa (she's originally from there) but goes back to Houston from time to time.

title: GOLDNRUSH PODCAST
difficultyExplanation: The podcast typically talks about the music industry and hip-hop world. As a result, references can sometimes make it hard to fully understand what is being discussed. However, it's still completely enjoyable even if you're not knowledgeable about that industry. The vocabulary is generally fairly simple overall, but slang is used quite frequently. This can vary depending on the guest, but conversations can also sometimes move at a fast pace.
description: Half-Japanese host somewhere in his low to mid 20s interviews people in the music industry as well as youtubers and other half-Japanese usually involved in music/hip hop.

title: After Hours
difficultyExplanation: Late-night podcast where two guys in their 20s talk about a variety of subjects.
description: A variety of topics spoken at casual but native speed. Pretty understandable but might be a rough as a first podcast.

title: 雑談72%
difficultyExplanation: Standard podcast targeted at natives with two men speaking. Great stepping stone from the easier podcasts.
description: Two men discussing everyday, slice of life topics, sports and sometimes simple news like the Olympics.

title: カワノユウマのマメトーク
difficultyExplanation: This is a podcast for natives and is not presented by a professional voice actor. He sometimes makes mistakes, uses filler words, and speaks at a normal pace for natives. The presenter is male and I believe is in his mid-late 20s.
description: This is a coffee podcast hosted by a roaster and cafe owner in Tokyo. The content ranges from what it's like to open up a business in Japan, to how to dial in different coffee brewing variables, stories about his trips to coffee growers around the world, and just enjoying/describing different coffees. He uploads weekly, there are 180 episodes, and most are about 20 mins long.

title: となりの雑談
difficultyExplanation: The transition between topics is not always very logical. Both speakers are well-educated and use complex vocabulary. Topics vary a lot. While it is still 雑談, it's as real as it gets.
description: Two women, one of them an author and the other a radio host. It feels like you're eavesdropping on them sitting in a café, talking about a really broad range of topics, often related to relationships and society. Subs

title: ジェーン・スー生活は踊る
difficultyExplanation: It can be a really challenging show, with no consistent theme/domain, but a brilliant wealth of listening material for natural speech and conversation.
description: Such a variety of topics are covered, that it's hard to summarise what the show is about; it is fundamentally anything to do with life, and lifestyle topics. It's lighthearted and entertaining while being aimed at adults, sometimes with serious advice for the お悩みコーナー、and is an excellent source of keeping up to date about day to day culture and life in Japan - currently trending foods, 便利グッズ、places to visit. Subs

title: Over The Sun
difficultyExplanation: They chat about any and all topics, and read messages from listeners, but many of their jokes and discussions can reference older Japanese trends and culture, as the focus is around 中年女性 lives, though they welcome anyone to listen in.
description: 「Over The Sun」 is another pure 雑談 podcast by ジェーン・スー and 堀井美香。 It's more upbeat and wild than となりの雑談、with lots of joking around. Subs

title: スーパニュートラルレディオショウ
difficultyExplanation: There are three different people, occasionally four if there's a guest, who are all from Kansai, so if you're not used to the goofy pitch and dialect phrasing, it may throw you off. You need to be focused on what is being said to avoid losing the thread of the conversation, there's occasional slang and cultural references. They sometimes talk over one another which makes it harder as well.
description: Random conversations with three hosts and sometimes a guest. They typically engage in random 雑談 and answer questions from viewers.

title: ゆる哲学ラジオ
difficultyExplanation: This is pretty complex due to the nature of explaining philosopy, and while they do try to explain the concepts, they talk somewhat fast and you will need a good understanding of decently complex vocabulary. Having some understanding of philosophy to begin with would definitely help.
description: Podcast meant to introduce philosophy to an adult, native audience. YouTube

title: ゆる言語学ラジオ
difficultyExplanation: Similar to the above, this is pretty complex but it is also definitely very, very interesting for Japanese learners, because you will learn a lot about the language.
description: Podcast meant to introduce grammatical and linguistic concepts to an adult, native audience. YouTube

title: 歴史を面白く学ぶコテンラジオ
difficultyExplanation: Complex subject matter, fast hosts that use slang, a lot of historical terms, very easy to lose the thread... This is hard, but also very rewarding.
description: Very interesting podcast discussing all sorts of historical episodes, and drawing parallels to contemporary societal issues and politics. YouTube
